QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_46

question.text: For an open-ended Cat III AIF, the MOST RELEVANT primary performance metric to report to investors in a monthly factsheet is:

answer.text: Internal Rate of Return (IRR) since inception

explanation.text: The Logic: Open-ended Cat III AIFs transact at NAV with continuous subscriptions and redemptions, so the natural performance metrics in monthly factsheets are NAV/unit (which lets investors compute their own return per subscription lot) and Time-Weighted Return (which neutralises investor cash flows and isolates manager performance for fund-vs-fund comparison). IRR, MOIC, and KS-PME are cash-flow-weighted metrics designed for closed-end private-equity vehicles where capital is called and distributed over time — not the typical Cat III open-ended monthly-factsheet metrics. The Trap: A, C, and D are metrics tailored to closed-end PE-style funds (often associated with Cat I/II AIFs), where IRR and money-multiple measures are more meaningful than time-weighted returns. None of them is a good fit for open-ended Cat III monthly factsheets. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (125, 156, 398, 452) support open-ended Cat III subscription/redemption mechanics and list TWR as a GIPS methodology, but do not explicitly designate "TWR + NAV/unit" as the primary monthly-factsheet metric for open-ended Cat III AIFs. The framing above is general industry practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
